questions.prompt: What does it mean that Vue is a "progressive framework"?

options.text: It only works with the newest browsers
You can adopt it incrementally — from one widget via a CDN up to a full build-tool app
It automatically upgrades your code to new versions
It must always be used with a backend server

questions.explanation: Vue is progressive: you can drop it into a page for a single interactive widget, or scale up to a full single-page application with a build tool — adopting only what you need.

questions.prompt: Which style does this course use for writing component logic?
questions.explanation: Both the Options API and the Composition API are fully supported, but this course uses the Composition API with <script setup>, the recommended default for new projects.

questions.prompt: Which of these are blocks in a single-file component (.vue file)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: An SFC bundles <template> (HTML), <script>/<script setup> (logic), and <style> (CSS). There is no <database> block.

questions.prompt: Vue automatically tracks which data the UI depends on and updates the DOM when it changes. This system is called ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Reactivity is the system that tracks data usage and re-renders the affected part of the UI when the data changes.

questions.prompt: Why can't a .vue single-file component run directly in the browser without tooling?

options.text: Browsers block .vue files for security reasons
SFCs must be compiled by a build tool like Vite into JavaScript the browser can run
SFCs only work on the server
They actually do run directly in every browser

questions.explanation: The .vue SFC format is compiled by a build tool (Vite) into standard JavaScript and CSS. The CDN build instead uses plain JavaScript component objects, which need no compilation.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its description.

pairs.right: Describe the UI for a state; Vue updates the DOM
Logic built from functions like ref and computed
A .vue file with template, script, and style

questions.explanation: Declarative rendering is the core idea; the Composition and Options APIs are the two logic styles; an SFC is the .vue file format that holds all three blocks.
